requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature. It MUST direct them to review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all the reviews running in parallel, before presenting any group to the user.
rationale:
structural: The requirement text states only what the skill document must direct agents to do. It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface. Every clause is about the skill's content, so the root `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is the thing being checked, not a structure it has to have.

I considered each clause as a structural obligation and found none:
- "put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature". A skill that gave the same direction in different wording would still satisfy this, so the wording is discretionary.
- "review every group with its own read-only subagent". This is a behavior the skill directs.
- "with all the reviews running in parallel, before presenting any group to the user". This is also a behavior the skill directs, and it is an ordering rule.

I read the root's Workflow section, and it contains the directions the requirement asks for. In `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md#section[Habeas%20requirements]/section[Workflow]/paragraph@1a08805c21f5` (step 3, Review):
- It sorts the new and changed requirements into groups that one reviewer should see together, meaning "requirements that cite each other or describe one feature".
- It tells the agent to start a read-only subagent for each group, "all in parallel".

The next step, `…/paragraph@7b764a629ec4` (step 4, Present each group to the user), comes after the reviews. It says the user is shown each group together with the design questions "the review returned", so the reviews finish before any group is presented.

Step 3 also lets the agent review the groups itself, one at a time, "If you can't start subagents". The requirement does not mention that case, and it is not a gap.

No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, and nothing is missing.

behavioral: The subject asks that the `habeas-requirements` skill direct agents to do four things:
1. Put each new or changed requirement into a group.
2. Define a group as requirements that cite each other or describe one feature.
3. Review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all the reviews running in parallel.
4. Do those reviews before presenting any group to the user.

The single marked test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_reviews_each_group_with_a_parallel_read_only_subagent]`, covers all four:
- `step_of(SKILL, "start a read-only subagent")` finds the workflow step. It panics if no step mentions a read-only subagent.
- `assert_text` checks that the step's whitespace-collapsed text contains "Sort the new and changed requirements into groups". This covers obligation 1.
- It checks for "requirements that cite each other or describe one feature". This covers obligation 2.
- It checks for "For each group, start a read-only subagent, all in parallel". This covers obligation 3: one subagent per group, read-only, in parallel.
- `assert!(review < step_of(SKILL, "Present each group to the user"))` covers obligation 4. It also panics if the presenting step is missing.

The helpers `workflow_steps`, `step`, `step_of` and `assert_text` do enforce these checks. `workflow_steps` parses the numbered steps and collapses wrapped lines, so the multi-line phrases in `SKILL.md` match. `assert_text` asserts that each phrase is present.

The bundled `SKILL.md` step 3 contains these phrases, so the test matches the shipped skill text.

I found no uncovered obligation, wrong expectation or ambiguity.
